data.summary: This 10‑week plan balances live class participation with focused self‑study, ensuring all AP Calculus AB units are covered. Each week includes a concrete task, a short focus line, and a realistic hour allocation that never exceeds the 5‑hour weekly limit. The final week is dedicated to mixed review and timed practice.

weeks.focus: Master foundational limits and derivatives with live guidance.
tasks:
Attend Class 1 (1.1) and take detailed notes.
Attend Class 2 (2.1) and solve the 5 practice problems posted.
Do 10 free‑response limit questions (1.2, 1.3) and grade using the rubric.
Review 5 algebraic limit problems (1.5) from the textbook.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of the Mean Value Theorem and basic integration concepts.
tasks:
Attend Class 5 (5.1) and complete the in‑class activity.
Read chapter on Riemann sums (6.1) and write a 200‑word summary.
Do 8 Riemann sum practice problems (6.2) and record errors.
Solve 3 MVT application problems and explain reasoning.

weeks.focus: Apply derivative rules to complex functions.
tasks:
Work through 10 power‑rule problems (2.5) and self‑grade.
Solve 5 chain‑rule exercises (3.1) and check solutions.
Complete 4 implicit‑differentiation problems (3.2) and peer‑review with a study partner.

weeks.focus: Explore related rates and motion contexts.
tasks:
Read related rates chapter and outline 3 example problems.
Solve 6 related‑rates questions (4.4) and annotate each step.
Model a straight‑line motion scenario (4.2) and compute velocity/acceleration.
Create a concept map linking derivative meaning to physical contexts.

weeks.focus: Investigate extrema and the First Derivative Test.
tasks:
Identify critical points for 5 functions (5.2).
Determine increasing/decreasing intervals (5.3) for each.
Apply the First Derivative Test (5.4) to classify extrema.
Summarize findings in a 300‑word report.

weeks.focus: Master the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and definite integrals.
tasks:
Translate 7 Riemann sum expressions into integral notation (6.3).
Compute 5 definite integrals using the FTC (6.4).
Create a cheat sheet of FTC steps.
Solve 3 word‑problem integrals and explain each step.

weeks.focus: Apply differential equations to real‑world modeling.
tasks:
Model a population growth scenario (7.1) and write the DE.
Verify a given solution (7.2) by substitution.
Sketch a slope field for the DE (7.3) using graph paper.
Write a short reflection on how slope fields inform solution behavior.

weeks.focus: Integrate applications: averages, areas, and motion via integrals.
tasks:
Compute the average value of 4 functions (8.1).
Relate position, velocity, and acceleration using integrals (8.2) for a given motion graph.
Find the area between two curves (8.4) for 3 pairs of functions.
Compile a worksheet of all solved problems for review.

weeks.focus: Consolidate knowledge with mixed practice and timed drills.
tasks:
Take a 60‑minute timed practice test covering all units.
Review incorrect answers and rewrite solutions.
Create a summary sheet of key formulas and theorems.
Discuss challenging problems with a tutor or peer group.

Do a full-length AP Calculus AB practice exam.
Mark the exam using the official scoring guide.
Identify top 5 weak areas and review targeted problems.
Restate the exam strategy and set a pre‑exam checklist.

data.final_week_advice: Prioritize sleep and light review the night before the exam; avoid cramming new material.
